attempts.text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"The Congressional Budget Office estimates that adopting a single-payer health insurance system could save in excess of $400 billion per year.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A single-payer national health system is the simplest, most efficient alternative to the current market-driven approach to health care delivery.", "claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Under a single-payer system, everyone receives a health care card giving them access to a wide range of health care services.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Out-of-pocket payments create barriers to access for the poor and add administrative cost to the health care system.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Under a single-payer system, hospitals are paid “lump sum” operating budgets.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[5]},{"claim_text":"Under a single-payer system, clinical staff’s time is no longer devoted to billing for every item administered but can instead be devoted to patient care.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[5]},{"claim_text":"Under a single-payer system, health insurance is no longer linked to employment or geography but instead follows the worker from job to job and from state to state.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[6]},{"claim_text":"Under a single-payer system, money for expensive technology is distributed according to a regional plan based on the needs of the local population.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[7]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
